key_insight: OUCH uses pneumatic actuation and concentrated contact geometry to deliver controlled wrist stimulation, eliciting discomfort at approximately 89% lower applied force than a handheld pressure algometer in preliminary testing.
engineering_relevance: A compact wearable could standardize stimulus delivery for neurological assessment by reducing variability in manually applied mechanical stimuli.
method: Stacked pneumatic pouch actuators drive a rigid indenter.
A compliant spacer buckles at a designed load, allowing skin contact only during actuation.
Finite element analysis and physical testing characterize force delivery and tissue deformation.
evidence_signal: Evaluation included blocked-force tests, clinician assessment, finite element analysis, a deformable testbed, and preliminary perceptual testing; at 200 kPa inflation, estimated contact pressure reached 18,500 kPa, over 25 times the algometer tip pressure.
watch_item: Preliminary discomfort results do not establish clinical assessment validity or safety for repeated use in patients with disorders of consciousness.
paper_title: OUCH: Objective, Uniform, Controlled Haptic Stimulation for Automated Neurological Assessment
